title: Fandisk (figure_10) fails in SnappingCarve.claimPassedVertex: two arcs run exactly through the same original mesh vertex
description: On master 0f52d26f, quad-layout on fandisk_in_tri.off (figure_10, 14454 faces, alpha 15) fails in the carve stage: `IllegalStateException: arc 879 runs exactly through copy vertex 684 (an original mesh vertex), which node -1 / arc 280 already holds; two T-mesh elements cannot share one mesh vertex`, thrown at SnappingCarve.claimPassedVertex (SnappingCarve.java:476) <- collectCrossings (:442) <- carve (:385) <- LayoutEmbedding.build (:123). Cross field (30 singularities), seamless, motorcycle graph and quantization all complete first. Found by the quad-layout mesh suite (Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite, baseline log tmp/quad-suite/master-0f52d26f/fandisk.log). Earlier fandisk tickets are DONE and were different failures: PATCH-109 (motorcycle NPE in ChartWalker.nextEdgeHit) and PATCH-115 (traces dying at degenerate chart cells). The closest past bug is PATCH-105 (buddha: recarve chord crossing a copy edge already held by an arc). Read how PATCH-105, PATCH-113 (bolt: copy elements claimed by two T-mesh elements) and PATCH-114 (hand: two nodes landing on one copy vertex) were fixed before choosing a fix: two arcs passing exactly through one original vertex is a degenerate-position case the carve must resolve (perturb, split, or route one arc around the vertex) rather than reject. The fix must follow the papers the embedding implements (Lyon 2021; Heuschling 2026 for layout embedding; Smith 2009 for robust inexact geometric predicates), cited at the change. Related: CRAW-70 (carve speedup) works in the same embedding/ package in parallel; keep the fix local to the degenerate case.
definition-of-done: 1. quad-layout on fandisk (alpha 15) completes the whole pipeline (through global grid map and patch surfaces) and renders a valid layout; screenshot under tmp/. 2. The fix addresses the degenerate exact pass-through generally, not just vertex 684 on fandisk, and a unit test reproduces the two-arcs-through-one-vertex case on a small fixture. 3. Whole-suite check: `python3 /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/run_suite.py --checkout <this worktree> --out /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/patch-fandisk --compare /home/acw/Code/Ixdar/tmp/quad-suite/master-0f52d26f` shows every other mesh MATCH (identical counts and screenshots; the fix must not change meshes that already work) and fandisk changing from load-failed to ok. 4. `ixd wt done` passes.
testing-plan: 1. Reproduce on master with run-scene --mesh fandisk. 2. Unit fixture for the degenerate pass-through. 3. Fix, rerun fandisk, screenshot. 4. Full suite compare against master.
unknowns: Whether arc 280's claim and arc 879's pass-through are both legitimate (a true degenerate position) or one of them is an upstream tracing error
changes-made: Diagnosis: reproduced on master 0f52d26f (tmp/logs/quad-layout-fandisk-1.log). Not a carve degeneracy but an upstream missed crossing. Arc 879 is trace 59 (axis V, u=-5.083662049942177, running -v) and arc 280 is trace 12 (axis U, v=-19.387086453692973, running -u). Trace 59 leaves source face 6251 exactly through its corner 2 and trace 12 leaves face 1439 exactly through its corner 1: both corners are mesh vertex 684 at chart point (-5.08366205, -19.38708645). The two iso-lines cross there transversally, so the crossing is legitimate (Lyon 2021 Sec. 3 requires a T-mesh node at it), but the four faces the two traces use around the vertex (6251/7798 and 1439/7064) are all different, and the motorcycle graph only finds crossings between chords lying in one face (FaceSegmentIndex), so it never noded the crossing. Both arcs then reach the carve still running through the vertex. No routing in the carve could fix this: the two arcs genuinely cross, so they must share a node there.

Fix (in progress, motorcycle package, not embedding/): (1) MotorcycleGraph.meetPassesThroughVertex records every exact pass of a trace through a mesh vertex (handleEdgeCrossing corner exits and crossStalledBoundary corner stalls) and nodes a perpendicular pass against every earlier pass of that vertex, exactly as handleIntersection nodes a chord crossing: one node pinned to the vertex through nodeAtChartPoint, a meeting with alpha on both traces, the other trace's direction carried into this face's chart by the new ChartWalker.quarterTurnsAroundVertex. Collinear passes are left to the existing head-on and covered-trace handling. (2) PatchBoundaryBuilder counted every hop through a node with vertexId >= 0 as a singularity corner, so the new crossing node on regular vertex 684 gave its patch 5 corners ('patch 447 is not a valid rectangle'). A node on a regular vertex (singularityIndex4 0, not critical, not border) is now flat when its two ports' unrolled-fan sort keys lie pi apart. Fandisk now loads end to end: '[motorcycle] arrangement patches: 832 cycles, 832 valid rectangles', traces=112 (covered=14) arcs=1706 nodes=876, '[embed] arcs=1706 copy V=11738 E=35208 F=23472', '[recarve] nodes=341 arcs=678 patches=339', global grid map 1.014s, patch surfaces 0.012s. Screenshot tmp/patch-126-after.png. Suite check and unit fixture next.

Whole-suite check (fixed runner, worktree code, vs master 0f52d26f): 12 of 14 MATCH (sphere_base, bolt, hand, elk, feline, fertility, botijo, block, rockerarm, buddha identical; Hand-tri-30k and crawfish fail identically). fandisk: load-failed -> ok (motorcycle arcs/nodes/patches 1708/877/831 -> 1706/876/832, completes through patch surfaces, global grid map 1.154 s). sphere_random: still fails with the same 'degenerate chart' error, but the fix finds vertex-pass crossings there too: motorcycle covered 14->16, arcs 1621->1623, nodes 903->907, patches 625->639. Waiting on a user ruling for the sphere_random change.
